section.content: The present disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting higher data transmission rates. Specifically, a method for selecting one or more User Equipments (UEs) for participation in an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) operation in a wireless communication system including an Application Function (AF), a network opening function (NEF), and a network data analysis function (NWDAF) is disclosed, including transmitting a first message from the AF to the NEF requesting assistance in UE selection and including member UE filtering criteria and specific parameters depending on the member UE filtering criteria, transmitting a second message from the NEF to NWDAF including an indication of a request depending on the specific parameters of the member UE filtering criteria and an end-to-end data volume transfer time analysis, transmitting a third message from NWDAF to the NEF including one or more analyses associated with the end-to-end data volume transfer time, deriving, by the NEF, one or more candidate UE lists meeting the member UE filtering criteria based on the analysis and the member UE filtering criteria, and transmitting a fourth message from the NEF to the AF including one or more candidate UE lists meeting the member UE filtering criteria.

本公开涉及一种用于支持更高数据传输速率的5G或6G通信系统。具体地，公开了一种用于在包括应用功能（AF）、网络开放功能（NEF）和网络数据分析功能（NWDAF）的无线通信系统中为参与人工智能/机器学习（AI/ML）操作选择一个或多个用户设备（UE）的方法，包括从AF向NEF发送用于请求UE选择辅助并包括成员UE过滤准则和取决于成员UE过滤准则的特定参数的第一消息，从NEF向NWDAF发送包括取决于成员UE过滤准则的特定参数和对端到端数据量传送时间分析的请求的指示的第二消息，从NWDAF向NEF发送包括与端到端数据量传送时间相关联的一个或多个分析的第三消息，由NEF基于分析和成员UE过滤准则导出满足成员UE过滤准则的一个或多个候选UE列表；以及从NEF向AF发送包括满足成员UE过滤准则的一个或多个候选UE列表的第四消息。

Member user equipment selection for artificial intelligence/machine learningTechnical Field

The present disclosure relates generally to wireless communication systems, and more particularly, to methods and apparatus for supporting member User Equipment (UE) selection, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) in third generation partnership project (3 GPP) fifth generation (5G) New Radio (NR) networks.

Background

In view of the development of wireless communication, technologies have been mainly developed for human-oriented services such as voice call, multimedia service, and data service. With the commercialization of 5G communication systems, it is expected that the number of connected devices will increase exponentially and will be connected to the communication network. Examples of connectivity things may include vehicles, robots, drones, home appliances, displays, smart sensors connected to various infrastructure, construction machinery, and factory equipment. Mobile devices are expected to evolve into various form factors such as Augmented Reality (AR) glasses, virtual reality head mounted devices, and holographic devices. In order to provide various services by connecting several billions of devices and things in the sixth generation (6G) era, efforts have been continuously made to develop an improved 6G communication system. For these reasons, the 6G communication system is called a super 5G system.

It is expected that a 6G communication system, which will be commercialized around 2030, will have a peak data rate of the order of bits per second (bps) of tera (1,000 giga) and a radio delay of less than 100 microseconds (musec), and thus will be 50 times faster than a 5G communication system, and have a radio delay of 1/10 thereof.

To achieve such high data rates and ultra-low delays, it has been considered to implement 6G communication systems in the terahertz (THz) band (e.g., the 95 gigahertz (GHz) to 3THz band). It is expected that a technology capable of securing a signal transmission distance (i.e., coverage) will become more critical since path loss and atmospheric absorption in a terahertz frequency band are more serious than those in a millimeter wave (mmWave) frequency band introduced in 5G. There is a need to develop, as a main technique of securing coverage, a Radio Frequency (RF) element, an antenna, a novel waveform having a better coverage than Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), beam forming, and massive Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO), full-dimensional MIMO (FD-MIMO), an array antenna, and a multi-antenna transmission technique such as a massive antenna. Furthermore, new technologies for improving THz band signal coverage have been continuously discussed, such as metamaterial-based lenses and antennas, orbital Angular Momentum (OAM), and reconfigurable smart surfaces (RIS).

In order to improve spectral efficiency and overall network performance, techniques have been developed for 6G communication systems for full duplex technology to enable uplink and downlink transmissions to use the same frequency resources at the same time, network technology for utilizing satellites, high Altitude Platforms (HAPS) etc. in an integrated manner, improved network architecture for supporting mobile base stations etc. and enabling network operation optimization and automation etc., dynamic spectrum sharing techniques through collision avoidance based on spectrum usage prediction, use of AI in wireless communication for improving overall network operation by utilizing AI from the design stage of developing 6G and internalizing end-to-end AI support functions, and next generation distributed computing technology for overcoming limitations of UE computing capabilities by ultra-high performance communication and computing resources available on networks such as Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), cloud etc. Further, by designing new protocols for 6G communication systems, developing mechanisms for implementing hardware-based secure environments and data security uses, and developing techniques for maintaining privacy, attempts are continuing to strengthen connectivity between devices, optimize networks, promote the software of network entities, and increase the openness of wireless communications.

It is expected that research and development of a super-connection 6G communication system including man-machine (P2M) and machine-to-machine (M2M) will realize the next super-connection experience. In particular, services such as true immersive augmented reality (XR), high fidelity mobile holograms, and digital replicas are expected to be provided through 6G communication systems. In addition, services such as tele-surgery, industrial automation and emergency response for safety and reliability enhancement will be provided through the 6G communication system, so that these technologies can be applied to various fields such as industry, medical, automobile and home appliances.

Documents that may be cited herein may include 3GPP Technical Specifications (TS) 22.261 (e.g., V19.5.0), 3GPP TS23.501 (e.g., V18.4.0), 3GPP TS23.502 (e.g., V18.4.0), 3GPP TS23.503 (e.g., V18.4.0), and 3GPP TS23.288 (e.g., V18.4.0).

In AI/ML operation, AI/ML models and/or data may be transmitted across AI/ML Applications (AF), 5G cores (5 GC), and UEs (including AI/ML servers in the UE). AI/ML operations can be divided into model training and reasoning phases during which multiple rounds of interaction may be required.

As described in 3GPP TS22.261 [1], certain AI/ML operation types can be divided into three types, model splitting, model sharing, and distributed/federal learning. The requirements, frequency and/or amount of data transmission may be different for different AI/ML processing stages and/or operation types.

In section 6.40 of 3GPP TS22.261 [1], the AI/ML model transfer describing the three types of AI/ML operations to be supported in release 18 is as follows:

AI/ML operation splitting between AI/ML endpoints

The AI/ML operation/model is split into multiple parts according to the current task and environment. The objective is to offload the computationally intensive, energy intensive parts to the network end points while leaving the privacy sensitive and delay sensitive parts on the end devices. The device performs the operations/models up to a specific part/layer and then sends the intermediate data to the network endpoint. The network endpoint executes the remainder/layer and feeds the reasoning results back to the device.

Distribution and sharing of AI/ML model/data over 5G systems

The multi-function mobile terminal may need to switch AI/ML models in response to task and environmental changes. The condition for adaptive model selection is that the model to be selected is available to the mobile device. However, given that AI/ML models are becoming more and more diverse, and due to limited memory resources in the UE, it may be determined that not all candidate AI/ML models are preloaded on-board. Online model distribution (i.e., new model download) is required, where AI/ML models can be distributed from NW endpoints to devices as needed by the devices to accommodate changing AI/ML tasks and environments. For this reason, it is necessary to continuously monitor the model performance at the UE.

Distributed/federal learning through 5G systems

The cloud server trains the global model by aggregating the local models trained in part by each terminal device. Within each training iteration, the UE performs training using the local training data based on the model downloaded from the AI server. The UE then reports the temporary training results to the cloud server via the 5G UL channel. The server aggregates the temporary training results from the UE and updates the global model. The updated global model is then distributed to the UE, and the UE may perform the training of the next iteration.

This section describes some 5GC enablers for supporting distributed/federal learning, model sharing, and model operation splitting AI/ML operations in the application layer.

An Application Function (AF) intended to provide AI/ML services to a UE may request 5GC assistance for federal learning, splitting AI/ML operations, etc., as described in section 5.46.2 of 3GPP TS23.501 [2 ]. The AF may subscribe to a network open function (NEF) by sending a target UE list, filter criteria, and other corresponding requirements for member UE selection. Based on the AF subscription information, the NEF may collect information and service data for the respective candidate UEs and determine UEs that can meet the filtering criteria and any other requirements. The NEF informs the AF of the list of candidate UEs that meet certain filtering criteria and requirements provided by the AF, as described in section 4.15.13 of 3GPP TS23.502 [3 ]. The candidate UE list may be dependent on the AF internal policy and final decision as a UE for this AI/ML operation.

During AI/ML operations (e.g., federal learning operations), the AF may update the filter criteria and/or target UE list to improve or maintain quality of service. This may be done for various reasons, such as if some UEs are unable to meet quality of service (QoS) requirements, if some UEs move out of the region of interest resulting in insufficient UEs to participate in AI/ML operation, if the UE's transmit time is unable to meet a required threshold, etc. Based on the update request of the AF, the NEF may update the candidate UE list and then inform the AF of the new candidate UE list meeting the requirements and/or inform the AF of any UEs that cannot meet the requirements.

Alternatively, depending on the operator policy, the AF may select a list of UEs for AI/ML operation (e.g. distributed/federal learning) without NEF participation, as described in (informative) annex I of 3gpp ts23.502 [3 ].

To more efficiently schedule AI/ML traffic and avoid 5G system (5 GS) congestion, an AF providing AI/ML services may negotiate with a 5GC a preferred time window for AI/ML operation (e.g., model transfer and/or inference data transfer) using the planned data transfer with QoS (PDTQ) requirements described in section 6.1.2.7 of 3gpp ts23.503 [4 ].

When AI/ML operation begins (e.g., when distributed/federal learning begins or is about to begin), the AF discovers the appropriate NEF and requests that the NEF provide QoS for a selected list of UEs, such as each UE identified by its UE Internet Protocol (IP) address, as described in section 4.15.13 of 3gpp ts23.502 [3 ]. For those AF QoS requests that result in successful resource allocation, AF may subscribe to QoS monitoring. The AF may provide one or more of QoS parameters, qoS profiles, qoS requirements, corresponding 5G QoS identifiers (5 QI), etc., derived from the performance requirements listed in section 7.10 of 3GPP TS22.261 [1 ].

As a result of subscribing to the NEF to provide a list of UEs meeting certain filtering criteria, the AF may be notified about the change in the list of candidate UEs. Accordingly, the AF may request a new preferred time window for AI/ML operation using scheduled data transfer with QoS, or may request to provide QoS with an updated list of UEs. Among the updated UEs, some may no longer require resource allocation, while some newly selected UEs may require resource allocation and QoS monitoring.

An AF intended to provide AI/ML operation (e.g., model sharing) may request assistance from the 5GC, as described in section 4.15.3.2.3 of 3GPP TS23.502 [3], by subscribing to NEF to be notified of the traffic (traffic volume) shared between the UE and the AI/ML application server. This may help the AI/ML application server determine how large the model is, and then, for example, select a large model less frequently than a small model.

The User Plane Function (UPF) may perform traffic detection for AI/ML traffic, as defined in section 5.8.2.4 of 3GPP TS23.501 [2], and the network may support charging for AI/ML traffic.

Network data analysis support.

In the 3GPP release (Rel-) 18 specification, the 5G system may support UE member selection assistance functionality to assist AF in selecting members/member UEs that are capable of participating in certain services (e.g., applying AI/ML operations, including federal learning, split learning/reasoning, reinforcement learning, etc.). The member UE selection assistance function may be hosted by the NEF. The member UE selection procedure is described in section 4.15.13 of 3GPP TS23.502 [3 ]. Features of the member UE selection assistance functionality hosted by the NEF include the following:

a request is received from the AF that should include a target member UE list (which is not necessarily part of a subsequent update request), one or more filtering criteria, as specified by table 4.15.13.2-1 in 3gpp ts23.502 [3] (e.g., UE current location, UE history location, UE direction, UE separation distance, qoS requirements, data Network Name (DNN), preferred access/Radio Access Technology (RAT) type, desired end-to-end (E2E) data volume transfer time performance or service experience), optionally, time window, etc.

With reference to the filtering criteria provided by the AF, and then interact with the 5GC Network Function (NF), the existing service is used to collect corresponding data of the target member UE list from the relevant 5GC NF (e.g., policy Control Function (PCF), network data analysis function (NWDAF), access and mobility management function (AMF), session Management Function (SMF)) to derive a candidate UE list (i.e., UEs in the target member UE list provided by the AF) that satisfies the filtering criteria.

The member UE selection assistance information is provided to the AF, including one or more candidate UE lists, and optionally other additional information (e.g., one or more recommended time windows for performing application operations, qoS for each target UE, UE location, access/RAT type, or service experience).

The procedure for member UE selection is specified in section 4.15.13.1 of 3GPP TS23.502 [3 ]. Referring to fig. 1 of the present disclosure (reproduction of fig. 4.15.13.1-1 of 3gpp ts23.502 [3 ]):

In step 105, the AF subscribes to the member UE selection assistance information by sending a first Nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _subscore request that includes a target member UE list, one or more member UE filter criteria as listed in Table 4.15.13.2-1, and optionally a time window. Subsequently, the AF may update only the subscribed member UE filtering criteria by invoking Nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _subscnibe and providing the subscription related ID, as described in section 4.15.13.0, i.e., the AF no longer provides the target member UE list.

In step 110, if the AF request does not contain a subscription related ID, the NEF verifies the authorization of the AF request and identifies which information needs to be collected for each UE in the target member UE list and performs the corresponding service operations, such as events, analysis IDs, notifications, etc., based on the member UE filtering criteria provided by the AF.

In step 115, if the AF request contains a subscription correlation ID, then NEF correlates Nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _Subscribe request with the existing subscription according to the subscription correlation ID. The NEF uses the target member UE received in step 1 to perform member UE updates using the updated filter criteria.

In step 120, the NEF interacts with different 5GC network functions to collect the information needed for each UE in the target member UE list. The set of interactions between NEF and 5GC NF depends on member UE filtering criteria provided by the AF. See Table 4.15.13.2-1 for details.

In step 125, based on the information collected from the other 5GC NFs, the NEF integrates all the information to derive a list of candidate UEs meeting the member UE filtering criteria in the AF request. The NEF may derive a recommended time window taking into account the validity period of the analysis for the member UE selection criteria. During the recommended time window, the candidate UE list may satisfy member UE filtering criteria. The recommended time window is a subset of the time window received by the AF. The list of candidate UEs meeting the member UE filtering criteria may be different in different recommended time windows.

In step 130, the NEF sends a Nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _notify request to the AF, including the candidate UE list and possibly additional information. See section 5.2.6.32.4 for details.

The NEF performs member UE selection assistance functions based on the AF request to determine one or more lists of UEs that meet and/or fail to meet the filtering criteria and any other requirements. The AF may consider the NEF's output and AF internal logic to determine the UEs and/or operating time windows that are involved in AI/ML operation.

The filtering criteria and corresponding procedures for member UE selection are specified in sections 4.15.13.2 to 4.15.13.6 of 3GPP TS23.502 [3 ]. The filtering criteria may include QoS requirements, access type or RAT type of Protocol Data Unit (PDU) session, E2E data volume transfer time analysis, UE current and historical location, UE separation distance, service experience analysis, and DNN.

If the AF sends the E2E data volume transfer time analysis as one of the filter criteria to the NEF, the NEF will subscribe to or send a request to NWDAF to obtain the corresponding output analysis. Disclosure of Invention

[ Problem ]

The present disclosure relates to wireless communication systems, and more particularly, to member UE selection for AI/ML in wireless communication systems.

[ Solution ]

It is an object of certain examples of the present disclosure to at least partially solve, process, and/or mitigate at least one problem and/or disadvantage associated with the related art, such as at least one of the problems and/or disadvantages described herein. It is an object of certain examples of the present disclosure to provide at least one advantage over the related art, such as at least one advantage described herein.

The invention is defined in the independent claims. Advantageous features are defined in the dependent claims. The embodiments or examples disclosed in the description and/or the drawings that fall outside the scope of the claims should be understood as examples that aid in the understanding of the invention.

According to one aspect of the present disclosure, a method for selecting one or more User Equipments (UEs) for participation in an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) operation in a wireless communication system comprising an Application Function (AF), a network opening function (NEF) and a network data analysis function (NWDAF) is provided, and the method comprises sending a first message from the AF to the NEF requesting assistance from the UE selection and comprising member UE filtering criteria and specific parameters depending on the member UE filtering criteria, wherein the member UE filtering criteria comprises an end-to-end data volume transfer time, sending a second message from the NEF to NWDAF comprising an indication of the specific parameters depending on the member UE filtering criteria and a request for end-to-end data volume transfer time analysis, sending a third message from NWDAF to the NEF comprising one or more analyses associated with end-to-end data volume transfer times, deriving by the NEF, based on the analysis and member UE filtering criteria, one or more candidate UEs meeting the member UE filtering criteria, and sending a list of candidate UEs from the NEF to the fourth message comprising a request for end-to-end data volume transfer time analysis, wherein the candidate UE filtering criteria comprises a number of data, a number of the UL filtering criteria and the target data transmission time, or the target items.

According to one aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a wireless communication system comprising an Application Function (AF), a network opening function (NEF) and a network data analysis function (NWDAF), wherein the wireless communication system is configured to send a first message from the AF to the NEF requesting UE selection assistance and comprising member UE filtering criteria and specific parameters dependent on the member UE filtering criteria, wherein the member UE filtering criteria comprises an end-to-end data volume transfer time; the method includes receiving, from the NEF to NWDAF, a first message including a request for end-to-end data volume transfer time analysis and specific parameters that depend on member UE filtering criteria, receiving, from the NEF to NWDAF, a second message including one or more analyses associated with end-to-end data volume transfer time, deriving, by the NEF and based on the analysis and member UE filtering criteria, one or more candidate UE lists that satisfy member UE filtering criteria, and receiving, from the NEF to the AF, a second message including one or more candidate UE lists that satisfy member UE filtering criteria, wherein the specific parameters that depend on member UE filtering criteria include one or more of a data volume of UL/DL data, a target number of data transmission repetitions, a target time interval between data transmissions, and a request for geographic distribution of UEs.

The following problems occur in the related art.

Problem 1

As described above, the data volume UL/DL and the request for geographic distribution of UEs (i.e., aoI) are two new and mandatory parameters for E2E data volume transfer time analysis in a NWDAF consumer's subscription or request. Furthermore, qoS requirements are mandatory filtering information for E2E data volume transfer time analysis. That is, NWDAF may collect service data from multiple NFs associated with an amount of data that is the same as/similar to/within the range of/less than or equal to the threshold value as the amount of data received from the consumer. NWDAF will use QoS requirements as one of the filters that output analysis reports.

Alternatively, the NEF may consider the QoS requirements of the service (AIML or federal learning service) in the QoS member UE filtering criteria as filtering information for NWDAF analysis of member UE selection. The NEF then informs NWDAF the corresponding QoS requirements to use as filtering information.

The NEF may support the E2E data volume transmission time filtering criteria using a request for geographic distribution of the UE (i.e., aoI) in other filtering criteria (i.e., UE current location, UE historical location, UE direction, UE separation distance, etc.).

The NEF may link/combine filter criteria in the same AF request (i.e., nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _subset) for member UE selection or the NEF may identify whether different member UE selection filter criteria are linked to the same service (AIML service) based on application ID, DNN, or other information in the filter information.

During member UE selection, the AF may indicate a time window for selecting candidate UEs in the Nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _subscore request. The time window for selecting candidate UEs is used by the NEF when subscribing/requesting to NWDAF. The NEF maps the time window for selecting candidate UEs to an analysis target period that should be included in Nnwdaf _ AnalyticsSubscription _substricribe or Nnwdaf _ AnalyticsInfo _request service operations.

Based on the AF request, the NEF collects and integrates the required data to derive UEs meeting the member UE selection filtering criteria. The NEF may also derive a recommended time window for service operation taking into account the validity period of the analysis for the member UE selection criteria. The candidate UE list may satisfy member UE filtering criteria within the recommended time window. The recommended time window is a subset of the time window received from the AF. The list of candidate UEs meeting the member UE filtering criteria may be different in different recommended time windows.

The NEF may also indicate a specific value of the parameters for the member UE filtering criteria that the NEF collects for each candidate UE and/or the number of UEs that cannot meet the filtering criteria (if there are multiple filtering criteria in the AF subscription request). The NEF may use this information to modify the corresponding filtering criteria to achieve optimal service operational performance by taking into account trade-offs between quality of service, UE and network conditions, number of UEs eligible to participate in the service (i.e., AIML service).

The UE and/or network conditions may vary significantly over different time windows or points in time, such as due to load and traffic changes of the network, services the UE and network are operating with, changes in control policies, and so on. There are some possibilities that only many UEs cannot meet certain filtering criteria within a minimum time window or point in time. In this case, the AF may not need to reduce the threshold/requirement of the filter criteria to produce more UEs that can meet the service operation requirements and reduce the quality of service. Instead, the AF may determine to discard some candidate time windows for operating the service. It would therefore be beneficial to inform the AF of the number of time windows or time points in which there are one or more UEs that cannot meet a particular filter criterion, or in which there are one or more UEs that cannot meet a particular filter criterion. However, in the prior art, the AF is unaware of the respective time window or point in time associated with the number of UEs that cannot meet this filtering criterion. The time window may be applied if the filtering criteria are related to the analysis output or if the filtering criteria are related to some real-time or historical data, i.e. QoS measurements, UE current location, UE historical location, etc.

The NEF may indicate the time window/point in time or the number of time windows to the AF, e.g. via Nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _notify or Nnef _ MemberUESelectionAssistance _notify service operation, along with specific values of existing parameters and/or the number of UEs.
